summary: Karl Schenkl worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna and studied under Georg Curtius. He held professorships at the universities of Innsbruck (1857–1864), Graz (1864–1875), and Vienna (1875–1899).

Karl Schönfeld was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Neuchâtel, Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn, and the University of Zurich under Adolf Kaegi, completing his Ph.D. in 1910. He taught at Kantonsschule Rychenberg from 1905 to 1928.

Karl Scriba, who worked in Indology and linguistics, studied at the universities of Munich and Berlin. He completed his PhD at the University of Würzburg by 1902 under doctoral supervisor Julius Jolly.

Karl Verner was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Aarhus Katedralskole, under August Leskien, and under Niels Ludvig Westergaard at the University of Copenhagen (Mag. 1873). He served as librarian in Halle (1876–1882) and Copenhagen docent (1882).

Karl Vilhelm Zetterstéen was a linguist who studied under Herman Almkvist and Eduard Sachau, earning his Ph.D. at Uppsala University (1895). He served as docent at Uppsala (1895) and Lund (1895–1904), and Professor of Oriental Studies at Uppsala (1904–1931).

Karl von Hegel worked in history and archaeology. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock from around 1841 to 1856 and at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from approximately 1856 to 1887.

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. After studying at Augsburg and earning a PhD at the University of Munich, he held posts at Munich (1978–1988) and as professor at Würzburg-Schweinfurt Technical University (1992–2014).

Tibetologist Karl-Heinz Everding earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (~1975–1985) and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg (1999), where he was Privatdozent in 1999. He later joined the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Karl-Heinz Gottmann was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied as a primary pupil under Anagarika Govinda from around 1952 to 1985 and succeeded him in 1982.

Working in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, Karl-Stéphan Bouthillette has held posts at the University of Munich, Laval University, the Research Foundation – Flanders, and Manipal Academy of Higher Education, with an assistant professorship at the University of Hong Kong (2026).
Karma Lek Shé Drayang pursued traditional studies under the guidance of teachers Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. She served as professor at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and Numata Professor at Hawaiʻi in 2023.

Karma Phuntsho specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Sera Monastery and Oxford (D.Phil. 2003 under Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich). His academic appointments include positions at CNRS, Clare Hall, and the University of Cambridge.

Karma Sonam Palmo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Tasmania under supervisors Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as abbot at the Young Lamas Home School (~1962–1965) and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery, and founded Kampo Gangra Drubgyud Ling and Tekchen Lekshay Ling.

Karma Ura works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at St. Stephen's College and Magdalen College, Oxford, and earned an MA from the University of Edinburgh. He was Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies (1999–2008).
Karmen Bašić was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Zagreb. From around 1993 to 1999, she served as the Executive Director of the Open Society Institute Croatia.
Karsé Kongtrul was a Tibetan Buddhist figure who studied under Khakyab Dorje (~1904–1924), the 13th Dalai Lama, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, the latter of whom he also taught.

Karthigesu Indrapala is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Jaffna College, the University of Ceylon, and under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1962–1965), later holding a post at the University of Tokyo (~1983–1984).

Karuna Kusalasaya was an active scholar in Indology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
